scope: Selected source-level boundary families; not an exhaustive static or dynamic call graph

rows.observation: One successful ReadAllBytes return counts the actual returned length; failed calls record unknown progress.
rows.remainingGap: Length metadata before the read is not counted; the API does not expose failed-read prefixes.
rows.prospectiveTreatment: Use returned-byte counters diagnostically; keep failures and metadata separate from bytes.

rows.observation: Four result reads in the real owner use decoded-text parse counters and raw returned-byte counters.
rows.remainingGap: Initial request/admission reads execute before the supervisor activates FILE_WORK. They are not included merely because they share the helper.
rows.prospectiveTreatment: Begin any future admitting enclosing timer before admission authentication; retain the present diagnostic scope label.

rows.observation: Harness JSON, counted streams, injected content readers, codecs and reconstruction counters cover selected reads/parses.
rows.remainingGap: Open/stat/close calls and all possible transitive library work are not established as an exhaustive application count.
rows.prospectiveTreatment: Use the enclosing time/job observation for broad scope; counters diagnose rather than replace that boundary.

rows.observation: Opt-in raw, parse, hash and decoder counters cover the independent auditor and selected compressed payload readers.
rows.remainingGap: Python imports, path checks, stat calls and full runtime activity are not counted as application operations.
rows.prospectiveTreatment: Retain raw/decoded/parser units separately and authenticate the actual modules used.

rows.observation: Existing parse counters cover explicit boundaries only.
rows.remainingGap: Native Copy serialize/deserialize round trips and canonical SerializeToElement work bypass those parse counters.
rows.prospectiveTreatment: Include this CPU/allocation work in an enclosing duration/memory boundary; do not infer time from counted parses alone.

rows.observation: The active Python owner counts directory-inventory calls, symlink/junction queries, storage lstat calls and final payload stat calls. Native writer leases count parent-directory ensure, exists and link-target calls.
rows.remainingGap: Other metadata paths remain unattributed. A completed API may return false or suppress errors; os.walk and File.Exists retain their existing behavior. These counters are neither complete enumeration nor storage peaks.
rows.prospectiveTreatment: Keep attempts, completed returns and thrown failures separate. Establish complete owned path and scratch domains before making a whole-process storage claim.

rows.observation: Two real exclusive DeleteOnClose handles use checked CloseHandle results in all modes. Opt-in acquisition and release counters retain their opening collector. Failure preserves a body exception with a cleanup note; success output/return follows release.
rows.remainingGap: A failed release leaves state unknown, never zero. A completed release is the API result, not a complete external file-lifetime or process-exit proof. Final archive receipts still precede cleanup; release failure adds failure.json and fails the supervisor.
rows.prospectiveTreatment: Bind cleanup outcomes and the full enclosing lifetime. Do not retry an uncertain handle release or admit an archive marked failed.

rows.observation: The same FileStream flags and contract are retained. Opt-in explicit Dispose/Close/DisposeAsync paths record release once against the acquisition collector. Expected acquisition rejection (sharing/lock violation) is a completed held-owner probe; release errors cannot satisfy the probe.
rows.remainingGap: Finalization is outside explicit release observations. Native using exception ordering is unchanged; failure state is unknown. Other protocols still have their own uninstrumented probe boundaries. No whole-process lease/scratch claim follows.
rows.prospectiveTreatment: Keep API acquisition failure separate from logical probe success. Include unresolved cleanup/finalization in a separately justified enclosing and scratch boundary.

rows.observation: Selected pending JSON, gzip and reservation-storage writers use pre-create declaration checks and append caps. Move/delete/directory publication verifies closed pending content and releases live bytes without refunding cumulative writes.
rows.remainingGap: Selected native and enclosing Python lease scopes are bounded through explicit cleanup. Hard elapsed-time guarantees, external/raw/metadata/alias operations, runtime/cache, finite observer work and resource qualification remain unresolved.
rows.prospectiveTreatment: Resolve runtime/cache, external domains and finite observer obligations; scientific gates stay closed.

rows.observation: ManagedStorage tracks exclusive managed-directory lengths; OwnerFileCounters observes copies, logs and lengths.
rows.remainingGap: SampledPeakTrackedFileBytes is a maximum of samples, not a process-wide high-water mark. Failed copies have unknown progress.
rows.prospectiveTreatment: Separate exclusive managed storage from sampled external storage and reject unknown members rather than assigning zero.

rows.observation: Enclosing job I/O observes operations but does not enumerate live filesystem storage.
rows.remainingGap: Transient files can grow and disappear between scans. Inherited environment/runtime paths are not an enforced private scratch namespace.
rows.prospectiveTreatment: Declare retained, pending, lease, log, scratch and runtime-cache domains; establish confinement or a separate conservative bound. Redirecting TEMP alone is insufficient.

rows.observation: V3 observes publication-observation persistence; supervisor sidecars retain observations through their own stated boundaries.
rows.remainingGap: Each final receipt excludes its own persistence. Job totals overlap application counters and are not additive.
rows.prospectiveTreatment: Use the enclosing owner job to observe child tails; preserve self-exclusions and terminal failure semantics.

rows.observation: The owner timer precedes supervisor.start, but file-accounting activation occurs after setup and initial hashes.
rows.remainingGap: validate/start raw reads, hashes and directory creation are not all attributed to owner application counters.
rows.prospectiveTreatment: A complete future outer boundary must include bootstrap work, not merely the four phase receipts.

rows.observation: Owned Windows jobs include native/Python descendants through drain, kernel transfer totals and job memory high water.
rows.remainingGap: Runtime/module loading and library operations lack exhaustive application attribution; monitor memory is sampled at a separate boundary.
rows.prospectiveTreatment: Do not add nested job totals, counters or separate lifetime memory peaks as though they were a simultaneous measured peak.

rows.observation: The original v1 owner observation keeps its exclusions. Opt-in monitor-call accounting additionally observes per-call preparation, child console sampling, publication and verification through the point before terminal snapshot construction.
rows.remainingGap: Constructor/earlier imports, terminal construction/persistence, caller console/process exit, outer-monitor memory lifetime and external/transient scratch are unresolved. A complete monitor call is not complete scientific or owner-process coverage.
rows.prospectiveTreatment: Bind the finite monitored set and a separately justified observer bound; keep terminal self-exclusions explicit. No recursive observer stack removes the need for a final bound.

rows.observation: Production code refreshes and rechecks required registry history; file/JSON helpers cover some reads.
rows.remainingGap: Future study cost depends on the full pinned history and metadata workload. Current correctness fixtures do not establish that workload bound.
rows.prospectiveTreatment: Include the actual admitted history closure in a future resource declaration; do not rescan or allocate in this inventory task.

rows.observation: Predeclared leaf roles and finite byte caps; source-bound retained owner integration; accepted append and deleted scratch lifetime accounting.
rows.remainingGap: Default owner/supervisor/native/process paths are not migrated. No OS confinement, external runtime/cache bound or completed observer lifetime.
rows.prospectiveTreatment: Use only for trusted single-owner diagnostics. Keep all whole-process/admission flags false until every required domain and observer has justified coverage.

rows.observation: Retained owner, supervisor publication and terminal publication all enforce declared names/roles/caps. Owner scope includes retained worker-sidecar copies. Final observation carries separate counters and declared aggregate upper bounds.
rows.remainingGap: Original sidecars and worker logs require separate optional declarations. Native pending/lease, runtime/cache and final terminal persistence/exit remain outside these managed directory scopes.
rows.prospectiveTreatment: Keep bounds restricted to the three disjoint directories. Never treat their cap sum or peak sum as an observed whole-process high-water mark.

rows.observation: Python/native per-file and aggregate original sidecar caps, failed-write poisoning, closed-length verification and owner-side length checks.
rows.remainingGap: Serialization memory, external mutations, native temporary files and remaining observer lifetime lack bounds. Worker logs have a separate opt-in contract.
rows.prospectiveTreatment: Use only as one named bounded domain. Keep all whole-process/admission flags false.

references.anchor: Bound all four persistent worker sidecars

rows.observation: Combined retained byte cap enforced before each parent write; original log handle is not inherited. Success requires EOF and verified closed length. Failure retains partial evidence and drains or rejects the owned job. Supervisor binds finite phase caps and rejects reuse.
rows.remainingGap: No bound on other paths, external log mutations, kernel pipe memory, worker output attempts or monitor console. Truncated, interrupted and write-failed captures cannot establish complete log capture.
rows.prospectiveTreatment: Keep retained-byte caps separate from overlapping process I/O and memory. Complete native pending/lease/cache and observer obligations before measurement.

Audit/publication prohibit leases. Authenticated v8/receipt-v5 observations validate member identity, role, attempt/release counts and unresolved state.

rows.observation: Authenticated two-path catalogue with one attempt each, finite concurrency and mandatory overlapping ownership through all workers. CREATE_NEW prevents deleting stale files. Original handles reject writes/resizes. Persisted observations require both releases, zero unresolved handles and no forced cleanup for success.
rows.remainingGap: Scope cleanup does not bound a hung owner, API call or outer observer. No filesystem confinement or complete external/metadata/alias/process-death coverage.
rows.prospectiveTreatment: Resolve runtime/cache and finite observer limits before prospective resource qualification.

prospectiveModel.elapsedBoundary: Before authentication through driver publication, verification, console and exit, with separately bounded outer-monitor work
prospectiveModel.memoryUnit: Explicit process/job commit high-water boundary; monitor separately identified
prospectiveModel.storageUnit: Logical retained plus scratch file bytes over declared complete lifetimes; not allocated disk blocks
prospectiveModel.ioUnit: Kernel job transfer totals; overlapping application bytes, decoded bytes and parser bytes remain separate diagnostics
prospectiveModel.failurePolicy: Unknown observations, failed release, missing membership, process escape or unresolved scratch prevent qualification; missing is never zero
prospectiveModel.cumulativePolicy: Charge all admitted attempts including failed work; never rewrite the first failure or historical totals
